question: What is the difference between a pointer and a reference?

scenes.sub: One is an object holding an address. The other is just a second name.
scenes.say: Pointer versus reference. Both let you reach another variable, but they behave very differently. One assignment shows it best.

scenes.head: One assignment tells them apart

panels.code:
int a = 10, b = 20;

int* p = &a;   // p stores a's address
int& r = a;    // r IS a

p = &b;        // p now points to b
r = b;         // copies 20 into a!

scenes.say: A pointer and a reference both start out at a. The pointer p is its own variable, holding a's address. The reference r is not a separate variable. It's just another name for a. Now watch. p equals address of b re-points p to b. But r equals b does not re-bind r. It copies twenty into a, because r is a, forever.

scenes.head: More rules

panels.code:
int* p;            // allowed (but dangerous)
int* q = nullptr;  // allowed: points to nothing
int& r;            // must be initialized
int& s = nullptr;  // no null references

int arr[3] = {1, 2, 3};
int* it = arr;
it++;              // pointer arithmetic: now at arr[1]

scenes.say: More rules. A pointer can be left uninitialized, or set to null. A reference must be bound when it's created, and can never be null. Pointers support arithmetic, like p plus plus, to walk through an array. References don't. You use a reference exactly like the original variable, with no stars or arrows.

scenes.head: Side by side
scenes.say: A pointer is a variable holding an address. A reference is another name for an existing object. Null: pointers can be, references can't. Re-pointing: pointers any time, references never. Initialization: optional for pointers, required for references. Arithmetic: only pointers. And syntax: pointers need star and arrow, references look like the object itself.

lines: Pointer: its own object storing an address. Nullable, re-pointable.
Reference: an alias. Never null, never re-bound, must be initialized.
Use references by default. Pointers when you need “nothing” or re-pointing.
scenes.say: A pointer is its own object that stores an address. A reference is an alias. Never null, never re-bound. Use references by default, and pointers when you need to represent nothing, or to re-point.
